Style: crisp polished pixel-art interface-world, strict orthographic top-down, no perspective and no isometric view. Theme: a digital reverse-engineering tower, the inside of a live binary program visualized as a navigable computing laboratory. Make the reverse-engineering identity unmistakable: large luminous 1s and 0s in long tidy streams on wall panels, giant segmented memory chips, PCB circuit traces, instruction-flow diagrams on vertical monitor arrays, and hexadecimal memory-like visual motifs. Restrict readable characters to binary 0 and 1 plus the exact requested floor label. Dark obsidian/navy surfaces and emerald phosphor glow, restrained amber lights, technical rather than generic factory or warehouse. No barrels, crates, rust, exposed plumbing, guns or combat. Geometry: a connected U-shaped broad EMPTY walkway starts at lower left around (12%,83%), runs left to right across the bottom at y=77%, turns up along far right at x=86%, then returns right to left across the top at y=26%. Keep top corridor x=8% to 92%, y=18% to 31%; bottom corridor x=8% to 92%, y=70% to 85%; right connector x=82% to 92%, y=18% to 85% clear and walkable. A central solid workstation island occupies x=8% to 78%, y=36% to 67%, separating top and bottom corridors. All machines, chairs and props stay on that central island or exterior wall edges, not on walkways. A small clearly glowing upward lift at upper left centered around x=11%, y=27% (tile 4,7); an arrival lift at lower left x=13%,y=84% (tile 5,23). Large low-contrast 0/1 floor circuit patterns can decorate clear walkways but must not appear to obstruct them. Outer walls around 5% margins. No people, no UI overlay, no grid, no extra words, no logo or watermark. Landscape aspect ratio 10:7. Floor 1 subject: source code and disassembly.
